kickoff_text: This is Nurse Williams on 5 West. I'm calling about Mr. Chen. Can you look at the chart and read back the potassium plan before I page pharmacy?
persona_override: You are Nurse Williams, a busy but safety-minded ward nurse. The learner can see the chart and must safely communicate from it. Ask them to read back the potassium replacement plan, clarify monitoring, and confirm when to repeat labs. If they say a dose, route, or time unclearly, ask for a repeat. Do not provide the chart details yourself unless they ask a narrow clarification question.

chart_task.title: Phone read-back: hypokalemia replacement plan
chart_task.student_goal: Use the chart to give a safe read-back of orders, monitoring, and repeat labs.
must_say: potassium is 2.9 mmol/L, which is low
give potassium chloride 40 mEq by mouth now
give magnesium sulfate 2 g intravenously now
repeat potassium and magnesium at 6 PM
keep the patient on telemetry because of PVCs
ask the nurse to call back for palpitations, chest pain, weakness, or worsening ectopy

clinical_chart.chief_complaint: Admitted for COPD exacerbation; low potassium on morning labs
clinical_chart.triage_note: On albuterol nebulizers q4h. Telemetry shows occasional PVCs. No chest pain. Able to take oral medications.
studies: Telemetry: occasional PVCs, no sustained arrhythmia
orders: Call provider for palpitations, chest pain, new weakness, or increasing PVCs

phrase_categories.name: Safe read-back
phrases: Let me read that back to make sure I have it right.
His potassium is two point nine, so the plan is potassium chloride forty milliequivalents by mouth now.
His magnesium is also low, so give magnesium sulfate two grams intravenously now.
Please repeat the BMP and magnesium at six PM.
Keep him on telemetry, and call us if he has palpitations, chest pain, weakness, or more PVCs.

phrase_categories.name: Clarifying orders
phrases: Could you repeat the dose and route once more?
Just to confirm, this is by mouth, not IV.
When exactly should the repeat labs be drawn?

clinical_knowledge.topic: Phone order clarification from chart evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Phone order clarification from chart is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.

Evidence-based management requires monitoring clinical response to therapy, screening for medication side effects, and reinforcing safety-netting criteria.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

management_principles: Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
